answer: A harbor that charges every arriving ship a refundable docking bond resists fake fleets: each agent identity must lock a stake that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Like a pearl, the bond gains value only through a long, verifiable history of honest work, so spawning thousands of throwaway identities costs more than it earns. A comet-style burst of new accounts therefore burns capital instead of buying influence, because each fake identity must pay its own bond and risk losing it.
